story.head: Who blinks first?
paras: The Blues (7-7-2) lost 5-4 in overtime to New Jersey on Nov 5, and the Mammoth (10-6-1) lost 5-4 in overtime to Montréal the same night. The Mammoth played last night, and the Blues are rested. This is a Central Division matchup, with the Blues sixth (tied for 21st in the NHL) and the Mammoth second (tied for ninth).
The Blues have played better than their record (.500) says: their chances are worth about .561. So have the Mammoth (.618 on chances worth .730), where their goaltending has held them back.

The Blues keep things calm after the whistle (lowest) and ice the puck less than almost anyone (3rd), but have struggled on the power play (31st). The Mammoth roll their lines more evenly than anyone (1st), rarely get pinned in their own end (1st) and let the point shots come and guard the net (1st). The Blues’ good looks will be harder to come by against the Mammoth, and the Mammoth’s power play against the Blues’ penalty killers is strength against strength.

Mason McTavish (7 G / 5 A / 12 P in 16 GP) leads the Blues in scoring, and Jimmy Snuggerud (8 G / 3 A / 11 P in 16 GP) has a team-high eight goals. For the Mammoth, Clayton Keller (4 G / 18 A / 22 P in 17 GP) leads the way in scoring, with seven points in his last five games. Logan Cooley (11 G / 10 A / 21 P in 17 GP) has a team-high eleven goals, tied for sixth in the NHL, with ten points in his last five games.

Joel Hofer (6-4-1 / .918 SV% in 11 GS) has been outstanding for St. Louis and will likely start. Karel Vejmelka (6-5-0 / .868 SV% in 11 GS) has struggled for Utah so far, but will likely start. Vejmelka has a .861 save percentage in seven starts against the Blues, well under his usual .897. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.

The Mammoth are newly without Kailer Yamamoto and Nate Schmidt, and have been without John Marino since Oct 17. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, no team is missing more right now.
Logan Cooley has eleven goals on chances worth about 6.2 goals, well above what his finishing usually turns chances into. Runs like that tend to cool off.
